topic: Dedekind cut of Q — lower-set convention
candidate_display_term: Dedekind cut of the rational numbers
candidate_context: Nonempty proper rational lower set with no greatest element
candidate_formulation: A Dedekind cut (lower-cut convention) is a set A⊂Q such that A≠∅, whenever a∈A and q∈Q satisfies q<a then q∈A, and for each a∈A there is b∈A with a<b.
mathematical_review: The nonempty/proper and no-greatest-element conditions are all essential for representing finite real numbers uniquely. The upward-cut and (lower,upper)-partition conventions are equivalent presentations only after a consistent endpoint convention is chosen.
prior_content_collision_check: Existing Dedekind completeness of arbitrary ordered set is not a Dedekind cut of Q; do not merge their meanings.

topic: Real numbers as rational Dedekind cuts
candidate_display_term: Dedekind-cut model of the real numbers
candidate_context: Concrete set model, distinct from an abstract complete ordered field
candidate_formulation: Let R_D be the set of all lower Dedekind cuts A⊂Q. For cuts A,B define A≤B exactly when A⊆B. The rational number q is represented by the cut {r∈Q:r<q}. With suitably defined addition and multiplication on cuts, R_D forms a complete ordered field.
mathematical_review: The representation q↦{r∈Q:r<q} is injective and order-preserving. Under strict lower-cut convention equality of real numbers is literal equality of cuts; abstract real field systems are isomorphic, not literally this set. Do not assert field/completeness without the separate proofs of operations.

topic: Least upper bound in rational Dedekind-cut model
candidate_display_term: supremum of bounded nonempty family of Dedekind cuts
candidate_context: Order is inclusion on real-number cut model
candidate_formulation: For a nonempty family S of Dedekind cuts that admits an upper bound cut, sup(S)=⋃{A:A∈S}.
mathematical_review: Nonemptiness makes the union nonempty. An upper bound B≠Q ensures the union is proper. Downward closure and the no-greatest-element condition pass to the union, so it is a cut and is the least upper bound by inclusion. The hypothesis S bounded above is required. This is not the definition of generic Dedekind completeness of any ordered set.

candidate_formulation: A sequence (a_n)_{n≥1} in Q is Cauchy if for every rational ε>0 there exists N∈N such that |a_m−a_n|<ε for all m,n≥N.
mathematical_review: Only the rational order, arithmetic, and absolute value appear in this definition; no real limit is assumed. Do not identify a Cauchy rational sequence with a rational limit because some lack one in Q.

candidate_context: Asymptotically vanishing difference in Q, without taking a real-number limit
candidate_formulation: For Cauchy sequences (a_n),(b_n) in Q, declare (a_n)∼(b_n) when for every rational ε>0 there is N such that |a_n−b_n|<ε for all n≥N.
mathematical_review: The difference a_n−b_n tends to zero in the already defined rational convergence sense. Reflexivity and symmetry are immediate; transitivity follows from the triangle inequality after splitting ε into halves. 'Same real limit' cannot serve as the definition because real numbers are not yet constructed.

topic: Real-number construction using rational Cauchy equivalence classes
candidate_display_term: Cauchy-sequence model of the real numbers
candidate_context: Quotient of rational Cauchy sequences by zero-difference equivalence
candidate_formulation: Let C_Q be the set of rational Cauchy sequences and ∼ the equivalence relation of eventual arbitrarily small rational difference. Define R_C=C_Q/∼. Its elements are equivalence classes [a_n], with [a_n]+[b_n]=[a_n+b_n], [a_n][b_n]=[a_n b_n], and q∈Q represented by the constant sequence (q,q,…).
mathematical_review: Arithmetic definitions must be shown independent of representative; this uses boundedness of Cauchy sequences and ε-arguments. A compatible total order must be built on classes, and Cauchy completeness and equivalence with least-upper-bound completeness need proofs. Do not define positivity of a class merely by eventually positive representatives: (1/n) represents zero.

topic: Positive real class needs eventual strict uniform positive bound
candidate_formulation: An equivalence class [a_n] is positive if some (equivalently, every) representative has a rational δ>0 and N such that a_n≥δ for all n≥N.
mathematical_review: The eventual positive margin δ, not merely pointwise positivity or eventual a_n>0, is necessary. A rational Cauchy sequence such as 1/n is positive in every term but belongs to the zero equivalence class. Representative independence follows by choosing ε=δ/2. The sum/product closure and trichotomy of resulting classes are separate results.
